sources.label: block.blockhash
sources.mechanism: Pre-Merge legacy: block proposer controls the nonce directly. Returns a constant on post-Merge Ethereum — still misused in forks and sidechains.
sources.note: Fully proposer-controlled. On post-Merge Ethereum it returns a predictable constant, so manipulation cost is effectively zero. Never use for security-sensitive randomness.
sources.useCase: Not recommended for any randomness use case on any network.

sources.label: PREVRANDAO
sources.mechanism: Beacon chain RANDAO accumulation (EIP-4399). Each slot proposer commits a BLS-signed reveal; the XOR accumulates. Proposer knows output in advance and can skip the slot to change ~1 bit.
sources.note: Skipping costs ~0.05–0.15 ETH (block reward + MEV). At ETH = $1,752 the break-even for an attacker is ~$88 of decision value per bit biased. Two cooperating validators can control 2 bits — enough to pick from 4 outcomes.
sources.useCase: Low-value decisions under ~$100 expected value. ε-greedy exploration in RL agents with small position limits. Always salt with keccak256(abi.encode(prevrandao, msg.sender, nonce)).

sources.label: Commit-Reveal
sources.mechanism: Two-phase protocol: participants commit a hash, then reveal the preimage. Output is XOR (or hash) of all reveals. No oracle required, but needs cooperative participants.
sources.note: Last-revealer trap: the final participant knows everyone else's contribution and can choose not to reveal at near-zero cost (only forfeits committed gas). Breaks for any dynamic agent strategy where optimal actions change during the reveal window.
sources.useCase: Fixed-set selection: lottery winners, NFT mint randomness, genesis parameters. Not suitable for agent strategy selection or any decision that depends on market state at execution time.

sources.label: Chainlink VRF v2.5
sources.mechanism: Threshold DKG: multiple Chainlink nodes jointly hold the VRF key; no single node can recover it alone. On-chain BLS proof verified by VRF Coordinator before delivery. Manipulation requires compromising the DKG threshold.
sources.note: Mainnet cost: 0.25 LINK ($2.01) + ~250k gas at 0.95 gwei ($0.42) = ~$2.43/request. Minimum 3-block confirmation window = 36s. On Base/Arbitrum: ~10–50× cheaper, ~$0.05–0.25. Batch up to 32 words per request at similar cost.
sources.useCase: Any agent decision with expected value above ~$500. Strategy switches, position sizing, randomized auction parameters. Use on L2 for high-frequency needs.

sources.label: Drand Beacon
sources.mechanism: Threshold BLS beacon (3s cadence) operated by Protocol Labs, Cloudflare, EPFL, Kudelski Security, and others. Outputs a BLS signature chain; each round is verifiable before use. No native Solidity SDK — requires an oracle bridge (Chainlink Functions or custom keeper).
sources.note: Public, free-to-read randomness with strong cryptographic guarantees. Oracle bridge adds 15–20s to the 3s cadence. No LINK fee, but bridge gas (~300k) still applies. No official Solidity SDK as of mid-2026; bridge liveness is a separate trust assumption.
sources.useCase: Cross-chain agents where LINK costs are prohibitive. High-frequency randomness (3s cadence beats VRF's 36s minimum). Teams willing to run a keeper or use Chainlink Functions as the bridge.
